q: 1. The contractor is responsible for
options: procuring material which is not supplied by the owner
organizing and planning the work as per drawing
executing the work as per specifications laid down in the contract
explain: A contractor's overall responsibility covers material procurement (where not owner-supplied), planning, and execution per specifications - all of the above.

q: 2. In the analysis of rate, the profit for the contractor is generally taken as
explain: In standard rate analysis practice, contractor's profit margin is conventionally taken as 15% of the cost.

q: 3. Contractor's prequalification is required for
explain: Prequalification is generally required only for major and specified/specialized works to ensure the contractor has adequate capacity and experience.

q: 4. Pre-tender stage requires
options: finalization of designs and preparation of estimate
explain: The pre-tender stage specifically requires finalizing designs and preparing detailed estimates before the tender is floated.

q: 5. Which of the following documents should be prepared and submitted by a contractor?
explain: The bid document is prepared and submitted by the contractor in response to a tender notice.

q: 6. The formula for determination of price adjustment in a work contract may not contain
explain: Price adjustment formulas typically use contract price, adjustment amount, and material/labour price indices, but do not directly include equipment cost as a variable.

q: 7. Bidding document is prepared
explain: Bidding documents must be finalized and prepared before the tender notice is published so bidders can obtain and use them.

q: 8. Security deposit deducted from contractor's bill is
options: refunded when the contractor has completed the work
refunded even before the completion of the work provided good progress has been established
retained till the expected life of the structure of say 100 years and spent for maintenance
refunded when the defect liability period is over
explain: Security deposit is retained as protection against defects and is refunded only after the defect liability period expires satisfactorily.

q: 9. During the construction period, price variation clause in contracts to
options: increase in rates of only important materials
variation in cost in materials element, labour element and petrol-oil-lubricant element
variation in total cost of the project on an adhoc basis
explain: Price variation clauses compensate for cost changes across materials, labour, and fuel (POL) elements during construction, not just important materials or an adhoc total figure.

q: 10. Mobilization advance upto 20 % of the cost of work is given to a contractor
options: on commencement of work at site for payment of loan taken by him
for the purchase of construction material
for the payment of advances to labour and other staff
for all activities required to start the work at site on finalization of contract document
explain: Mobilization advance is granted to help the contractor cover all initial startup activities (equipment, materials, staff) needed to begin work at site after contract finalization.

q: 11. Direct purchase can be done for construction work when the amount is
explain: Per public procurement regulations, direct purchase (without formal bidding) is permitted for works valued up to Rs. 0.3 million.

q: 12. Pre-Qualification document should be approved by
explain: D would have been the beast answer but AS PER BOOK A .Depending on the level and type of public entity, pre-qualification documents can be approved by the Director General, chief of public entity, or a class-I gazetted office chief - any of the above.

q: 13. A document containing detailed description of all the items of work (but their quantities are not mentioned) together with their current rates is called
explain: A schedule of rates lists item descriptions and their current unit rates without specifying quantities, unlike a tender document or estimate.

q: 14. A contractor can start the construction works following the receipt of:
explain: The formal 'notice to proceed' is the document that authorizes the contractor to actually commence construction works at site.

q: 15. The tender is
options: Written offer submitted by contractor to execute works
explain: A tender is the written offer submitted by a contractor proposing to execute the specified works at quoted rates/terms.

q: 16. The pre-tender stage of construction requires:
explain: The pre-tender stage involves site selection, land acquisition, and design finalization - all necessary before floating the tender.

q: 17. According to "Contract Act 2055" the number of classes of contractor are
explain: The Nepal Contract Act/Public Procurement regulations categorize contractors into four classes: A, B, C, and D.

q: 18. Earnest money is a .......towards the execution of a public tender government contract.
explain: Earnest money is a deposit submitted by bidders as a guarantee of serious intent to execute the contract if awarded.

q: 19. Pre-tender stage requires
options: selection of site and acquisition of land
finalisation of designs and preparation of estimate
explain: Before a tender is called, the owner must secure the site, finalize the design, and prepare a cost estimate to ensure the project is ready for bidding.

q: 20. During construction, price variation clause in a contract applies to:
options: increase in cost of important materials only
variation in the cost of materials, labour and fuel
variation in total cost of the project estimated and a lump-sum figure
explain: Price variation clauses cover changes in the cost of materials, labour, and fuel (POL) elements during construction execution.

q: 21. Which types of tender generally prefer
explain: Schedule of Rates (SOR) is preferred in civil engineering works as it allows for payments based on actual quantities measured at agreed rates.

q: 22. Within the relationship among client, engineer and contractor, no agreement is required between
explain: The engineer typically acts as the client's representative under the main contract; no separate formal agreement exists directly between the engineer and the contractor.

q: 23. Whle filling the tender for any work, the contractor considers quotation?.
explain: Site conditions, labor pricing, and technical specs are critical inputs when pricing a bid[cite: 1].

q: 24. While filling the tender for any work, the contractor considers quotation?
explain: A contractor must evaluate the site conditions, labor market, and technical requirements (specifications) to provide an accurate and competitive price.

q: 25. Tender is awarded for
explain: In competitive bidding, the contract is typically awarded to the lowest responsive and responsible bidder who meets all technical requirements.

q:
26. Tender is called for
i) to minimize the cost of an item
ii) to find exact rate of item of unknown item
iii) to take minimum rate from contractor
explain: Tenders invite open competition to minimize work costs and obtain competitive rates from contractors[cite: 1].

q: 27. Tender is called for i) to minimize the cost of an item ii) to find exact rate of item of unknown item iii) to take minimum rate from contractor
explain: Tendering promotes competition to ensure the owner receives the most economical price (minimum rate) for the work.

q: 28. Which of the following information is generally not published in a tender notice?
explain: Performance bond requirements are typically specified in the contract document rather than published details in the initial tender notice.

q: 29. Local tender is not favorable due to following reasons:
options: most of the material used locally
engineer or site in charge pressurized
explain: Local tenders can sometimes lead to localized pressure or influence on the decision-making staff compared to international competitive bidding.

q: 30. If a contractor is found corrupt for tender work then what should be done by the concerned office
explain: Corruption leads to administrative actions like cancellation, financial penalties, and potential legal prosecution.

q: 31. Quality and cost based selection (QCBS) method is used
options: Progress of work up to a stage
explain: QCBS is a standard method used to select consultants by evaluating both technical quality and cost of their proposals.

q: 32. Tender document does not contain
explain: The unit rates are filled in by the contractor during the bidding process; the blank document itself does not provide them.

q: 33. The amount of earnest money generally deposited at the time of submission of tender is
explain: Earnest money deposit (bid security) is typically fixed at 2% to 3% of the estimated project cost[cite: 1].

q: 34. The amount of earnest money generally deposited at the time of submission of tender is
explain: In Nepal's Public Procurement Act, bid security (earnest money) is usually 2% to 3% of the estimated amount.

q: 35. A turn key contract is offered for
explain: A turnkey contract involves the contractor handling every stage from design to completion so the owner can 'turn the key' and start using the facility.

q: 36. Amicable settlement means
explain: Amicable settlement is a non-adversarial process where the parties resolve the dispute themselves through negotiation.

q: 37. By using the method of sealed quotation, which of the following cannot procured?
options: all of the above can be procured
explain: The sealed quotation method can be used for procurement of works, goods, and services alike - so all of the above can be procured.

q: 38. A contractor can start the construction works following the receipts of
explain: The 'Notice to Proceed' is the formal authorization that marks the official start date of the project.

q: 39. The purpose of bid evaluation is to determine
explain: Bid evaluation aims to identify the lowest evaluated bid among those that are substantially responsive to the tender requirements.

q: 40. While making the agreement of any contract, the legal authority is appointed by
explain: A single entity (the owner/client) typically establishes the legal framework for the contract document.

q: 41. What are the essential components of a valid contract?
explain: An enforceable contract mandates mutual offer/acceptance, free consent, legal capacity, and consideration[cite: 1].

q: 42. The post tender stage of construction consists of
explain: The post-tender stage includes work assessment, expenditure tracking during execution, and final account settlement - all these activities.

q: 43. The types of contract followed in Middle-Marsyangdi hydro electricity project is
explain: Major public civil engineering works like hydro projects typically utilize item rate contracts[cite: 1].

q: 44. The money of the contractor retained by the department during payments is called :
explain: Retention money is a percentage withheld from progress payments to ensure the contractor completes the work and fixes defects.

q: 45. The types of contract followed in Manmohan Memorial Polytechnic Institute (Hatimuda, Morang) is
explain: This institution complex project was awarded as a turnkey design-build construction contract[cite: 1].

q: 46. Force majeure in contract is:
options: occurrence of an act beyond the control of both the parties
preventing both parties to perform the respective obligation agreed
explain: Force majeure refers to 'Acts of God' or unforeseeable events that make contract fulfillment impossible through no fault of the parties.

q: 47. Force majeure in a contract is
options: occurrence of an event beyond the control of both the parties of the contract
occurrence of an event beyond the control of the contractor
occurrence of an event beyond the control of the employer
explain: Force majeure refers to unforeseeable events beyond the control of both contracting parties (e.g., natural disasters), excusing performance delays.

q: 48. The price of tender document for the bidding amount upto two crore is (Source:PPR2064(48))
explain: According to Nepal PPR 2064 Rule 48, standard bid document fee up to NRs 2 crore is NRs 3,000[cite: 1].

q: 49. Generally in GoN office, what is the main intention of Office Chief
explain: While bidding is the legal standard, office chiefs often prefer direct purchase for smaller, urgent requirements due to speed.

q: 50. The amount of VAT for the purchase of steel having an amount of NRs. 6000/- should be
explain: VAT in Nepal is 13%. $6000 \times 0.13 = 780$.
